Job Description:
DePuy Synthes, the orthopedics business of Johnson & Johnson, is recruiting for a North America Transport Operations Lead (M1), preferably based in Raynham, with remote as an alternative location in North America.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate its Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal and regulatory requirements. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes, and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans.

Purpose of the Position
The North America Transport Operations Lead (M1) is a key member of the global supply chain function, responsible for operational management of the transportation network across the North America region, including importation from global sites in other regions.
The role ensures the reliable, cost-efficient, and fully compliant movement of products — from manufacturing sites and regional hubs into local distribution centers, hospitals, and distributors — while safeguarding adherence to customs and international trade regulations across all operating countries.
This is a single regional leadership position that brings together two closely related disciplines: how products physically move (transportation networks, carriers, logistics providers) and how they cross borders compliantly (customs, import/export, trade documentation). The role partners closely with regional and global stakeholders enable uninterrupted product flow, mitigate risk, and drive continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
- Drive value across North America through optimized regional transportation flows for both inbound freight (from manufacturing sites and global hubs to regional hubs, and from hubs to local affiliates and distributor warehouses).

- Manage relationships with third-party and fourth-party logistics providers (including global Control Tower partners) through performance metrics, strategic direction, and continuous improvement programs.

- Support further deployment, development and maturity of the Global control tower in the North America region

- Lead performance measurement of transport reliability through critical metrics aligned with regional Plan, Make, and Deliver operations teams; provide input into executive performance reviews.

- Deliver on annual cost improvement and productivity targets through operational improvements while protecting service, quality, reliability, and compliance.

- Translate regional inventory strategy and business requirements into innovative transportation solutions; support transportation set-up for manufacturing network changes and new product launches.

Cross-Functional Leadership
- Partner with regional and global supply chain, Trade Compliance operations, Quality, finance, and legal teams to enable compliant product movement and rapid issue resolution.

- Represent transportation in end-to-end supply chain forums, projects, and sales and operations planning discussions; drive process alignment and trade-off decisions.

- Actively collaborate with the regional Deliver lead, distribution operations, and demand & supply planning teams to optimize capacity planning, reliability, and adherence to service commitments.

- Support product launches, network changes, and supply chain transformations by assessing and managing transportation impacts.

Key Objectives / Metrics
- Transportation cost and continuous improvement savings delivery.

- Transportation reliability — manufacturing/hub to distribution center, and distribution center to customer.

- Logistics provider (Control Tower) performance against agreed service levels and value creation targets.

Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor's degree required (Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, International Trade, or related field).

- Master's degree or MBA preferred.

Required Experience and Skills
- 6–8 years of progressive experience in supply chain, transportation, trade compliance, logistics, or related operational roles, aligned with a manager-level position.

- Strong working knowledge of international trade, customs regulations, and import/export operations within North America.

- Solid expertise across core transportation, planning, and carrier / logistics-provider management, including familiarity with control-tower operating models.

- Excellent analytical skills and an affinity for numbers: ability to support budgeting, financial reconciliation, and identify cost-saving opportunities in transportation.

- Good understanding of the order-to-cash process and end-to-end supply chain mindset.

- Experience partnering with global stakeholders and operating within a matrixed, multinational organization.

- Proven ability to manage complex operational issues, assess risk, and drive compliant outcomes.

- Effective communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills across cultures and geographies.

Preferred Experience and Skills
- Experience in medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or other highly regulated industries.

- Familiarity with global trade systems, transportation management systems, enterprise resource planning platforms, and transport & trade visibility & automation tools.

- Demonstrated experience leading regional or global process standardization initiatives.

- Understanding of good distribution practice and a quality-first approach.

DePuy Synthes, a ~$9 billion business, has an outstanding opportunity for a Senior Finance Manager operating within Supply Chain Finance to gain extensive exposure across DePuy Synthes Principal Operations while leading the Currency Management team.
Role Overview
In this role, you will provide financial leadership to the Currency Management team, leading the identification and management of foreign currency exposures, centralized hedging, hedge and inventory accounting, forecasting, analytics and reporting across DePuy Synthes.
You will play a critical role in standing up the group to operate as a standalone DePuy Synthes Principal Operations team, ensuring that essential currency management activities continue to be performed to the highest standards of compliance, accuracy and insight before, during and after separation.
The immediate focus of the role will be to stand up the Currency Management team and its operating model; establish the end-to-end exposure identification, hedge submission, accounting and control processes required to support placement of hedges through a third-party provider; and lead the development and ongoing maintenance of replacement calculation and analytics capabilities as existing systems will not be available to DePuy Synthes following separation.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead, coach and develop a global team of three finance professionals.
- Serve as the first point of contact for currency-related topics and questions across DePuy Synthes.
- Lead the identification and management of foreign currency exposures, including centralized forecasting and balance sheet hedging, and establish the process required to place hedges with a third-party provider.
- Ensure accurate and compliant hedge and inventory accounting in line with US GAAP and relevant accounting procedures.
- Lead the calculation, analysis, reporting and communication of actual and forecast transactional currency impacts across DePuy Synthes P&L lines, including driver-based variance analysis, trends, risks and opportunities.
- Provide currency analytics, insights and recommendations to DSPO, FP&A, Treasury and senior management.
- Lead regular currency and hedge-result reviews with business partners and senior leadership and provide training and educational materials to strengthen understanding of currency and hedging principles across DePuy Synthes.
- Lead the design, build, testing and deployment of a replacement tool to support currency calculations, hedging, analytics and reporting, and oversee its ongoing maintenance and enhancement.
- Drive standardized and efficient processes through automation and analytics tools, including Power BI and Alteryx.
- Partner across DSPO, Treasury, Tax, FP&A, Technology and Project Osprey teams to stand up the Currency Management team and ensure continuity of critical activities through separation.

Qualifications and Experience
- Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably with a major in Accounting, Economics or Finance; a Master’s degree, MBA or recognized financial qualification such as ACA, ACCA or CIMA is preferred.
- Minimum of 7 years of finance, accounting or related business experience.
- Demonstrated leadership capability, with the ability to develop others, support organizational health and remove barriers to success.
- Strong analytical skills and proven ability to bring clarity to complex business issues, manage complex projects and processes, and translate complexity into practical solutions.
- Excellent communication and business partnering skills, including the ability to frame complex data, simplify written communications, influence internal customers and work effectively with all management levels.
- Confident presenting to senior management, facilitating discussion and providing clear recommendations and solutions.
- Ability to operate independently in a dynamic, high-visibility global environment, manage competing priorities and collaborate effectively across a virtual matrix organization.
- Strong continuous improvement mindset; Supply Chain experience and proficiency with TMI, Alteryx or Power BI are preferred.
- Demonstrated understanding of AI concepts and frameworks, including awareness of responsible and ethical AI practices, and has experience generating effective prompts to boost efficiency and productivity.

Leadership Capabilities
- Leads and develops talent through coaching, delegation and clear accountability.
- Builds trusted relationships and influences effectively across a global organization.
- Combines strategic thinking with strong execution, prioritization and attention to detail.
- Demonstrates integrity, resilience and a strong continuous improvement mindset.

- Provide proactive insights on risks, opportunities, trends, and financial impacts related to compensation, benefits, headcount, and workforce costs.
- Challenge assumptions and influence decision-making through data-driven recommendations and scenario analysis.

- Provide clear and concise storytelling of financial results, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions to stakeholders.
- Support quarterly business reviews, leadership discussions, and strategic planning sessions.

Actuals & Financial Close Support

- Partner with accounting and operational teams to investigate variances and resolve issues impacting financial results.
